Create a slope chart.

Source: R/slope_chart.R
slope_chart.Rd

A slope chart (or slopegraph) compares two values per category by placing them on two vertical axes, typically "before" and "after" or two years, and connecting them with a straight line. The steepness and direction of each line show at a glance which categories rose, which fell, and how their ranking changed. The form was popularised by Edward Tufte in The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (1983) and is a staple of the New York Times graphics desk.

Each line is labelled with its category name and value at both ends; labels that would overlap are nudged apart vertically. Lines can be colored by direction (increase, decrease, no change), a subset of categories can be emphasised with highlight, and hovering over a line fades the others.

Usage

slope_chart(
  data,
  start,
  end,
  group,
  startLabel = NULL,
  endLabel = NULL,
  colorByDirection = TRUE,
  upCol = "#1a9850",
  downCol = "#d73027",
  flatCol = "#888888",
  lineCol = "steelblue",
  highlight = NULL,
  mutedCol = "#cccccc",
  lineWidth = 2,
  circleRadius = 4,
  showValues = TRUE,
  digits = NULL,
  labelFontSize = 11,
  headerFontSize = 13,
  title = NULL,
  titleFontSize = 16,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bgcol = "white",
  axisCol = "black",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The data frame containing the variables to consider, in wide format (one row per category).

start

The name of the numeric column holding the values plotted on the left axis.

end

The name of the numeric column holding the values plotted on the right axis.

group

The name of the column holding the category labels (one line per category).

startLabel

Header displayed above the left axis. Defaults to the value of start.

endLabel

Header displayed above the right axis. Defaults to the value of end.

colorByDirection

Whether to color lines by direction of change (upCol, downCol, flatCol). If FALSE, every line uses lineCol. Defaults to TRUE.

upCol

Color of lines that increase. Defaults to "#1a9850".

downCol

Color of lines that decrease. Defaults to "#d73027".

flatCol

Color of lines with no change. Defaults to "#888888".

lineCol

Color of all lines when colorByDirection = FALSE. Defaults to "steelblue".

highlight

Optional. A character vector of categories (values of the group column) to emphasise. All other lines are drawn in mutedCol. Defaults to NULL (no emphasis).

mutedCol

Color of non-highlighted lines when highlight is used (their labels are drawn semi-transparent). Defaults to "#cccccc".

lineWidth

Width of the lines in pixels. Defaults to 2.

circleRadius

Radius of the end-point dots in pixels. Defaults to 4. Use 0 to hide the dots.

showValues

Whether to print the value next to each category label. Defaults to TRUE.

digits

Optional. Number of decimal places used to print the values. Defaults to NULL, which prints the values as they are.

labelFontSize

Font size of the category and value labels. Defaults to 11.

headerFontSize

Font size of the two axis headers. Defaults to 13.

title

Optional. Title of the chart.

titleFontSize

Font size of the chart title. Defaults to 16.

font

The font family used for all text. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bgcol

Background color of the SVG. Defaults to "white".

axisCol

Color of the two vertical axes, the headers, the title and the labels. Defaults to "black".

width

Optional. The width of the SVG output.

height

Optional. The height of the SVG output.

Value

An SVG slope chart.

Examples

# Current receipts of government as a percentage of GDP, 1970 vs 1979
# (adapted from Edward Tufte's classic slopegraph)
receipts <- data.frame(
  country = c("Sweden", "Netherlands", "Norway", "Britain", "France",
              "Germany", "Belgium", "Canada", "Finland", "Italy",
              "United States", "Greece", "Switzerland", "Spain", "Japan"),
  y1970 = c(46.9, 44.0, 43.5, 40.7, 39.0, 37.5, 35.2, 35.2, 34.9, 30.4,
            30.3, 26.8, 26.5, 22.5, 20.7),
  y1979 = c(57.4, 55.8, 52.2, 39.0, 43.4, 42.9, 43.2, 35.8, 38.2, 35.7,
            32.5, 30.6, 33.2, 27.1, 26.6)
)

slope_chart(
  data       = receipts,
  start      = "y1970",
  end        = "y1979",
  group      = "country",
  startLabel = "1970",
  endLabel   = "1979",
  digits     = 1,
  title      = "Government receipts as % of GDP",
  height     = 520
)



# Life expectancy in 1952 vs 2007, highlighting two countries
library(gapminder)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

countries <- c("China", "India", "Japan", "Brazil", "Nigeria",
               "Egypt", "Germany", "United States", "South Africa")

life <- filter(gapminder, year %in% c(1952, 2007), country %in% countries)
life <- select(life, country, year, lifeExp)
life <- pivot_wider(life, names_from = year, values_from = lifeExp,
                    names_prefix = "y")

slope_chart(
  data       = life,
  start      = "y1952",
  end        = "y2007",
  group      = "country",
  startLabel = "1952",
  endLabel   = "2007",
  highlight  = c("China", "South Africa"),
  digits     = 1,
  title      = "Life expectancy: 1952 vs 2007"
)
